title: Certified naturality and the obstruction to unrestricted naturality in a typed two-dimensional calculus
abstract: We formalize the boundary of naturality in the labelled conversion calculus of A Theory of a Two-Dimensional Typed Lambda Calculus. Canonical evaluation of inductively presented homotopies constructs naturality squares, and transport along finite presentations preserves two-paths and recovers the naturality boundary. In contrast, an explicit pointwise family on Fin 3 admits no naturality two-cell or finite pasting: a six-element dihedral-group invariant separates its two boundary paths while respecting every declared two-cell generator. This independently reconstructed refutation is classical, not a verification of the manuscript's claimed constructive Idris proof. Supporting results distinguish beta and eta evidence by parity and give a standalone typed de Bruijn syntax with exact raw-tree representation adequacy and a parity-preserving conversion interpretation. The result concerns this declared evidence calculus, not normalization, full abstraction, or a completeness theorem for lambda calculus.
